title: Protected Resource Metadata
description: RFC 9728 discovery, where the server advertises its authorization server through a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge and clients follow it rather than being configured by hand.
question: Does the framework discover the authorization server from the challenge?
why: This is what makes connecting to an unfamiliar protected server possible without out-of-band setup. A framework that requires hand-configured endpoints cannot connect to a server it was not told about in advance, and cannot handle a step-up scope challenge when one arrives.
known_issues: Measured with the official MCP conformance suite 0.1.16, whose client scenarios are tagged 2025-11-25.

notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73, an OAuthClientProvider as the HTTP transport's authProvider, conformance suite 0.1.16): discovery passed in metadata-default, var1 and var2. In metadata-var3, where the authorization server's URL has a path, the client also requested that server's metadata at the root path (authorization-server-metadata-wrong-path, 5 of 8 checks passed).
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: No auth hook (see Authorization): the workbench never fetches protected-resource or authorization-server metadata.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` takes only static `headers` or a `header_provider` and builds its HTTP transport with `auth=None`, so it never fetches protected-resource or authorization-server metadata.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `StreamableHttpServerInfo` and `SSEServerInfo` take a static `token` or `headers`, and `MCPClient` builds its httpx client with no auth handler, so the adapter does no OAuth discovery: it never fetched the protected resource metadata or the authorization server metadata in the conformance suite's auth scenarios.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: the starter has no OAuth hook; Spring AI points OAuth users at the separate community module `mcp-client-security`. Against the conformance auth scenarios the client sends no Authorization header, never fetches protected-resource metadata, and fails to start on the server's 401.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPServerHTTP` and `MCPServerSSE` take only `url` and static `headers`, and `HTTPTransport` calls `streamablehttp_client` with no `auth`, so the client does no OAuth discovery: in the conformance suite's auth scenarios it never fetched the protected resource metadata or the authorization server metadata.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `StreamableHttpServerParameters` and `SseServerParameters` take only static headers, and ADK has no OAuth hook. Every `auth/*` conformance scenario fails: the client sends no `Authorization` header, the server answers 401, and `McpToolset.getTools` throws `McpToolLoadingException` (cause: `McpHttpClientTransportAuthorizationException`).
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `StreamableHttpMcpTransport` takes static `customHeaders` or an `McpHeadersSupplier`, and langchain4j-mcp ships no OAuth client. It never fetches protected-resource or authorization-server metadata.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no OAuth flow, so the client never requests protected resource metadata or authorization server metadata after the 401.
